chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from al-Amriki ibn Ali, who said: Yahya narrated to us, and he was in the service of Abi Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), from Ali, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in a long hadith of his.

He said: I asked, 'What is the reward for one who prays near him — meaning al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'Whoever prays two rak'ahs near him, Allah, the Exalted, will grant him whatever he asks for.'

I asked, 'What is the reward for one who performs ghusl with the water of the Euphrates and then goes to him?' He replied, 'If he performs ghusl with the water of the Euphrates with the intention of going to him, his sins will fall away from him as on the day his mother gave birth to him.'

I asked, 'What is the reward for one who sends provisions for him but does not go himself due to an illness?' He replied: 'Allah will give him for every dirham he spent [in sending others] good deeds equal to the weight of Mount Uhud, and He will compensate him with multiples of what he spent, and divert from him afflictions that had descended, so they will be repelled, and his wealth will be preserved.' And he mentioned the hadith in its entirety.

key_terms.جَبَلِ أُحُدٍ: Mount Uhud (used as a measure of weight/volume for good deeds)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for praying or performing ghusl near the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the metaphysical efficacy of the Karbala shrine, framing it as a locus of divine grace where physical proximity or even financial delegation yields spiritual purification. The promise that sins drop off like the day of birth upon ghusl with Euphrates water underscores the river's sanctity in Shia tradition, while the multiplication of rewards for those who send representatives illustrates the concept of *khulaf'* (substitution) in devotional acts.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. My father narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, and from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā Al-‘Aťťār, from ‘Amraki ibn ‘Ali, from Yaḥyā – the servant of Abī Ja’far the Second (Imam Jawād (a.s.)), from ‘Ali, from Safwān Al-Jammāl, who said: I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) – as part of a longer Ḥadīth, –

“What is the reward for those who establish prayers next to him – referring to Ḥusain (a.s.)?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Those who establish two Rak’ah of prayers next to him will not ask anything from Allāh, the Exalted, without Allāh granting it.”

I asked, “What about those who perform Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates (River) and then go to him?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “If they perform Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates (River) with the intention of going to him, their sins will fall off of them (and they will become sinless) like the day their mothers gave birth to them.”

I asked, “What about those who make arrangements for others to go but they do not go themselves because of being ill?” Imam (a.s.) replied: Allāh will recompense them for every Dirham that they have spent (making the arrangement for others) with rewards as great as the mountain of Uḥud and will sustain them with multiple amounts. Furthermore, the afflictions which had been destined for them will be pushed away and their wealth will be protected.
